title: Interorgan Metabolic Cycles
objectives: Describe the major nutrient exchange pathways between organs
Explain the role of key metabolites in interorgan communication
Identify clinical disruptions in metabolic cycles
Analyze diagnostic patterns in metabolic cycle disorders

introduction.title: Principles of Interorgan Metabolism
introduction.content:
The human body coordinates metabolism through specialized cycles between:

  • Liver (Biosynthesis/detoxification)
  • Muscle (Energy consumption)
  • Adipose (Energy storage)
  • Brain (Priority fuel allocation)

cori_cycle.title: Glucose-Lactate Cycle
cori_cycle.content:
Cori Cycle
• Muscle: Glucose → Lactate (anaerobic glycolysis)
• Liver: Lactate → Glucose (gluconeogenesis)
Regulators: NAD+/NADH ratio, oxygen availability
Key Enzyme: Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH)
Isoforms: LDH1 (heart), LDH5 (liver/muscle)
Diagnostic use: ↑LDH5 in muscle injury

alanine_cycle.title: Glucose-Alanine Cycle
alanine_cycle.content:
Muscle
• Pyruvate + amino group → Alanine
• Transports nitrogen to liver
Liver
• Alanine → Pyruvate (via ALT)
• Pyruvate for gluconeogenesis
• Nitrogen enters urea cycle

Clinical correlation: Elevated ALT in liver damage

ketone_metabolism.title: Liver-Brain Ketone Cycle
ketone_metabolism.content:
Ketogenesis (Liver)
• Substrate: Acetyl-CoA from β-oxidation
• Products: β-hydroxybutyrate/acetoacetate
• Regulator: Malonyl-CoA inhibition
Ketolysis (Brain)
• Converts ketones back to acetyl-CoA
• Provides >60% brain energy during fasting

clinical_relevance.title: Clinical Disruptions
clinical_relevance.content:
Diabetic Ketoacidosis

Mechanism: Uncontrolled lipolysis → excessive ketogenesis

Diagnosis: ↑β-hydroxybutyrate, anion gap metabolic acidosis

Treatment: Insulin + hydration

Reye's Syndrome

Cause: Mitochondrial dysfunction during viral illness

Effect: Disrupted liver-brain metabolite exchange

Marker: ↑Ammonia with normal amino acid levels

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Why can't muscles perform gluconeogenesis during the Cori cycle?

Muscles lack glucose-6-phosphatase, the final enzyme required to release free glucose into circulation. This ensures muscles retain glucose-6-P for local glycolysis.

How does the alanine cycle protect against ammonia toxicity?

By transporting amino groups as stable alanine (non-toxic) rather than free NH4+, preventing neurotoxicity during muscle protein catabolism.

Why do ketone bodies require less oxygen to metabolize than fatty acids?

Ketones bypass the rate-limiting carnitine shuttle system and β-oxidation steps, providing acetyl-CoA directly to the TCA cycle with lower oxygen demand.
